title: Bequest
description: A disposition of property or money in a will. Supports 8 core types (specific, pecuniary, demonstrative, general, residuary, life_interest, class, debt_forgiveness) and extension types via x-inherit- prefix (e.g. x-inherit-wasiyya, x-inherit-halachic-matanah)
$comment: Life interest bequests require lifeInterest object.

allOf.$comment: Core types (specific, pecuniary, demonstrative, general, residuary, debt_forgiveness) require beneficiaryId OR beneficiaryOrganisation.

id.description: Unique identifier for this bequest within the INHERIT document

bequestType.description: The category of bequest. Core types cover common law estates. Extension types use x-inherit- prefix (e.g. x-inherit-wasiyya, x-inherit-halachic-matanah)
bequestType.$comment: specific: a named item to a named person. pecuniary: fixed cash sum. demonstrative: cash from specified fund. general: from general estate. residuary: remainder. life_interest: right to use/benefit during lifetime. class: to a category of people. debt_forgiveness: cancellation of a debt owed to the testator.

beneficiaryId.description: Reference to the Person.id of the individual beneficiary

beneficiaryIdDisplay.description: Human-readable display name for the referenced beneficiary

beneficiaryOrganisation.description: Organisation receiving this bequest, if not an individual

classDefinition.description: Natural-language definition of the beneficiary class. Required for class bequests. Must be precise enough for executors to identify all members
classDefinition.$comment: Natural-language description of the class of beneficiaries (e.g. 'All my grandchildren living at my death').
examples: All my grandchildren living at my death
My children in equal shares
The children of my late brother Ahmed
The descendants of my sister Lakshmi
The children of my late uncle Kwame

lifeInterest.description: Life interest details, required when type is 'life_interest'

amount.description: Cash amount for pecuniary and demonstrative bequests, in minor currency units

sharePercentage.description: Percentage share of the residuary estate or a specified fund

description.description: Free-text description of the bequest — what is being given
examples: My engagement ring and matching necklace
The entire contents of my wine cellar
All my shares in Acme Ltd

sourceAssetId.description: Reference to the Asset.id from which a demonstrative bequest should be paid
sourceAssetId.$comment: For demonstrative bequests — the asset from which the amount should be paid.

conditions.description: Conditions precedent that must be satisfied before the beneficiary receives this bequest. Each condition has a typed category for machine-readable common patterns, plus a human-readable description
conditions.$comment: survival_period: beneficiary must survive the testator by a specified number of days (e.g. 30-day survivorship clause). age_attainment: beneficiary must reach a specified age. event: a specific event must occur (e.g. graduation, marriage). marriage: beneficiary must be married at the relevant date. residence: beneficiary must reside in a specified location. employment: beneficiary must be employed in a specified role or industry. custom: free-text condition not covered by other types — use description field

description.description: Human-readable description of the condition, as expressed in the will
examples: Beneficiary must survive me by 30 days
Beneficiary must have attained the age of 25

survivalDays.description: Number of days the beneficiary must survive the testator. Only applicable when conditionType is survival_period

attainmentAge.description: Age the beneficiary must reach. Only applicable when conditionType is age_attainment

personId.description: The person this condition applies to, if different from the bequest beneficiary

failureConsequence.description: What happens if this condition is not satisfied

failureDescription.description: Human-readable description of the failure consequence

substitutions.description: Substitute beneficiaries in case the primary beneficiary cannot receive the gift

hotchpot.description: Whether lifetime gifts (advances) to the beneficiary are brought into account when calculating their share. Common in intestacy and some wills
hotchpot.$comment: Whether lifetime gifts to the beneficiary should be brought into account when calculating their share.

distributionMethod.description: How the bequest is distributed among multiple beneficiaries
distributionMethod.$comment: per_capita: each beneficiary receives an equal share. per_stirpes: shares pass by representation. modified_per_stirpes: like per_stirpes but sharing begins at first generation with living members. per_capita_at_each_generation: shares at each generation divided equally among living members and descendants of deceased members.

predeceaseRule.description: What happens if the beneficiary dies before the testator
predeceaseRule.$comment: lapse: gift fails if the beneficiary predeceases the testator — falls into the residuary estate. per_stirpes: passes to the predeceased beneficiary's issue by representation. substitution: passes to a named substitute beneficiary. accrual: redistributed among surviving co-beneficiaries of the same gift. statutory_default: the jurisdiction's default rule applies (e.g. s.33 Wills Act 1837 in England and Wales).
examples: per_stirpes
lapse

constrainedBy.description: Which legal principle constrains this bequest, if any
constrainedBy.$comment: testamentary_freedom: testator may dispose of this gift freely. customary_rule: customary law constrains or overrides this bequest. forced_heirship: civil law forced heirship rules constrain this bequest. religious_rule: religious law constrains this bequest (e.g. wasiyya limited to one-third). coparcenary_survivorship: Hindu coparcenary property passes by survivorship, not by will.
examples: testamentary_freedom
forced_heirship

customaryOverride.description: Whether customary or religious law overrides the testator's freedom to dispose of this gift as they wish
customaryOverride.$comment: Whether customary/religious law overrides testamentary freedom for this bequest.

postDeathActions.description: Post-death actions that modified this bequest — disclaimers, deeds of variation, appropriations

inheritanceResponse.description: The beneficiary's formal response to this inheritance, if applicable

hotchpotTransferIds.description: References to lifetime transfer IDs that should be brought into account (hotchpot) when calculating this beneficiary's entitlement. Links bequests to prior gifts — if the testator gave the beneficiary £50,000 during their lifetime, this bequest may be reduced accordingly

notes.description: Free-text notes about this bequest. Use for context, testator intent, or special instructions to executors
examples: This ring has been in the family for four generations — please ensure it stays in the family
If the charity has merged or changed name, the executor should identify the successor organisation

assetIds.description: References to Asset.id(s) being bequeathed as individual items. A bequest may reference either assetIds (individual items) or assetCollectionId (entire collection), not both

assetCollectionId.description: Reference to the AssetCollection.id being bequeathed. A bequest may reference either assetIds (individual items) or assetCollectionId (entire collection), not both

propertyIds.description: References to Property.id(s) being devised. Links this bequest to specific real property — enables programmatic estate distribution calculation
propertyIds.$comment: Connects bequests to the properties array. A specific devise of 'my house at 42 Elm Street' should reference the Property entity. Validated at Level 2 for referential integrity

liabilityIds.description: References to Liability.id(s) associated with this bequest. For debt_forgiveness bequests, these are the debts being cancelled. For other types, indicates liabilities attached to the bequeathed asset
liabilityIds.$comment: Enables structured debt forgiveness modelling (Phase 2) and asset-encumbrance tracking. A bequest of a mortgaged property should reference both the Property (via propertyIds) and the Liability (via liabilityIds)

insurancePolicyIds.description: References to InsurancePolicy.id(s) associated with this bequest. Links life insurance or other policies whose proceeds form part of this gift

charityPurposeRestriction.description: Restriction on how the charity may use the bequeathed funds — e.g. 'Must be used for cancer research only'
examples: Must be used for cancer research only
For the upkeep of the church building

charityNonMergingClause.description: Whether the gift fails if the charity merges with another organisation before distribution

charityReportingRequired.description: Whether the charity is required to report back on how the funds were used

charityGiftAidEligible.description: Whether the bequest has been verified as eligible for Gift Aid. In the UK, estates leaving 10%+ to charity qualify for the reduced 36% IHT rate

charityRegistrationVerifiedAt.description: When the charity's registration was last verified as active

legacyPledge.description: A legacy pledge commitment tracked before the will is finalised

pledgeAmount.description: Pledged amount in minor currency units

pledgeDocumentId.description: Reference to a Document.id recording the pledge

fundingAssetId.description: Asset backing the pledge, if funded

giftAidRegistrationNumber.description: Gift Aid registration number for the charity

giftAidVerificationUrl.description: URL to verify the Gift Aid registration

giftAidVerifiedAt.description: When Gift Aid registration was last verified

authorPersonIdDisplay.description: Human-readable display name for the referenced author person

provenance.description: Consolidated provenance metadata — how this entity was created, by whom, and whether a human has verified it

applicableLaw.description: The jurisdiction whose succession law governs this item. Missing means defaults to estate domicile

powerOfAppointmentId.description: Reference to a PowerOfAppointment.id — indicates this bequest's distribution is subject to a power of appointment

classSubstitution.description: Substitution rules for class gifts — what happens when a member of the class predeceases the testator

substituteClass.description: Who takes the share of a deceased class member
examples: children of deceased class members

priority.description: Explicit priority order within the will. Lower numbers take precedence

clauseReference.description: The clause number in the will that contains this bequest
examples: clause 4
paragraph 7(a)

executorDirections.description: Administrative directions to the executor regarding this bequest

directive.description: The instruction as expressed in the will
examples: Receipt of the authorised officer shall be a sufficient discharge
My executor shall sell the property within 12 months of probate

mentionedAssetIds.description: Assets mentioned in this clause for clarity but not limiting scope. For residuary bequests, named for legal certainty while absorbing all unallocated assets

mentionedPropertyIds.description: Properties mentioned in this clause for clarity but not limiting scope

precatoryWishes.description: Non-binding wishes expressed by the testator about how the beneficiary should use or treat the bequeathed item

wish.description: The wish as expressed in the will
examples: I express the wish that she keep it as a family heirloom

BeneficiaryOrganisation.description: An organisation that receives a bequest — charity, company, trust, or unincorporated association

examples: British Red Cross
Manchester University
Médecins Sans Frontières

type.description: The legal form of the organisation
type.$comment: charity: registered charity. company: limited company or corporation. unincorporated_association: club, society, or group without legal personality. trust: a trust entity. other: any organisation type not covered above.

registrationNumber.description: Charity registration number, company number, or other official registration

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction where the organisation is registered

LifeInterest.description: Details of a life interest — one person enjoys the asset during their lifetime, then it passes to the remainderman

tenantForLifeId.description: Reference to the Person.id who holds the life interest

tenantForLifeIdDisplay.description: Human-readable display name for the referenced tenant for life

remaindermanId.description: Reference to the Person.id who receives the asset after the life interest ends

remaindermanIdDisplay.description: Human-readable display name for the referenced remainderman

remaindermanClassDefinition.description: Natural-language description of the remainderman class if not a named individual
examples: All my grandchildren living at the death of the life tenant, in equal shares

interestType.description: The scope of the life interest
interestType.$comment: use_and_income: right to use the asset and receive any income it generates. income_only: right to income only, not physical use. use_only: right to occupy or use, but no income entitlement. protective: a protective trust — converts to discretionary trust if the life tenant attempts to assign their interest. right_of_residence: right to live in the property for life.
examples: use_and_income
right_of_residence

Substitution.description: A substitute beneficiary who receives the bequest if the primary beneficiary cannot (e.g. predeceases the testator)

beneficiaryId.description: Reference to the Person.id of the substitute beneficiary

beneficiaryIdDisplay.description: Human-readable display name for the referenced beneficiary

classDefinition.description: Natural-language description of the substitute class
examples: The children of the deceased beneficiary, in equal shares

beneficiaryOrganisation.description: Substitute organisation if the substitution is to a charity or company

condition.description: The condition that triggers this substitution
examples: If my daughter predeceases me
If the primary beneficiary disclaims the gift

perStirpes.description: Whether the substitution is per stirpes — passing to the deceased beneficiary's descendants by representation

PostDeathAction.description: An action taken after death that modifies the bequest — disclaimer, deed of variation, appropriation, or assent

type.$comment: disclaimer: beneficiary formally refuses the gift. deed_of_variation: beneficiary redirects the gift to another person (within 2 years of death in the UK for IHT purposes). appropriation: executor transfers a specific asset to satisfy the bequest. assent: executor formally vests the asset in the beneficiary.

examples: Deed of variation redirecting £50,000 to grandchildren's trust
Beneficiary disclaimed life interest in favour of children

documentId.description: Reference to the Document entity recording this action

variationDetails.description: Details of a deed of variation — who redirected what to whom

InheritanceResponse.description: The beneficiary's response to the inheritance — acceptance, renunciation, or qualified acceptance. In civil law jurisdictions, acceptance may be required within a time limit

response.description: The beneficiary's formal response to the inheritance
response.$comment: accepted: beneficiary has accepted the inheritance. renounced: beneficiary has formally renounced — the gift lapses or passes to a substitute. qualified_acceptance: beneficiary accepted with limitations (e.g. accepting only up to the value of assets, not liabilities — common in Japan and France). pending: no response yet — may be within the statutory response period.

responsePersonId.description: Reference to the Person.id of the respondent

responsePersonIdDisplay.description: Human-readable display name for the referenced response person

courtFiled.description: Whether the response was filed with a court (required in some jurisdictions)

deadlineDate.description: Statutory deadline for responding (e.g. 3 months in Japan, 4 months in France)
